textbookText: Figure: 9.3.4 Soil Pollution Soil is an important abiotic component of environment where all living beings and micro organisms thrive. Throwing and dumping wastes into the soil from various sources deteriorate the natural quality and originality of soil. Soil pollution is defined as any undesirable changes Biology, Grade 11 | 464
in the physical, chemical and biological aspects of soil. Soil pollution alters texture, fertility and water holding capacity of soil.

1. SOURCES a. Domestic wastes Wastes produced from houses such as plastics, rubber, unused food materials, dust, waste paper, tin cans, excreta of animals, broken pieces of utensils, glasses, unused agricultural products etc. are dumped into the soil. Such condition diminishes soil fertility. This situation also favours growth of pathogenic micro-organisms and spread to nearby residential areas causing epidemics. b. Municipal wastes In urban area, wastes such as plastic, leather, paper, glasses etc. produced from hospital, offices, houses, schools, colleges, and streets etc. which are collected by municipality. Such wastes consist of both degradable and non-degradable waste and they should be separately managed and dumped. If not, organic content in soil and heavy metal content like Cu, Pb, Cr, Ni etc will increase. c. Wastes from industries Various types of industries such as paper and pulp industries, food processing industry, soap and detergent factory, pharmaceuticals, mining industries produce various biproducts at the time of manufacture of goods. Bi-product or wastes produced are sulphide, bleaching liquors, pathogens, polyphosphates, drugs, mine wastes, suspended solids, chloride, and heavy metals etc. which are released to external environment causing soil pollution. d. Biocides and chemical fertilizer Biocides are the chemicals used to kill insects, pest, mite, fungi and rodents which destroy our cultivated crops and annoy us. They are of various types such as, insecticide, pesticide, rodenticide, fungicides and so on which include DDT, aldrein lindane, parathion, toxaphane. Farmers also use different types of chemical fertilizers in the field to enhance crop production. Nowadays, maximum and haphazard use of pesticides and chemical fertilizer caused soil pollution. e. Physical disturbances Unplanned irrigation schemes, building construction, atomic explosion, and deforestation have resulted soil pollution which lead to soil erosion, expansion of deserts and scanty rainfall. f. Acid rain Air pollution causes acid precipitation in the environment which is of two types- dry precipitation and wet precipitation. Many chemicals including acid particles, gases etc. either remain in air or settle down on the soil or any hard surfaces which is called dry precipitation. During rainfall, such acidic gases or particles dissolved in water forming acid and fall back on soil. g. Radioactive wastes Nuclear dust and radioactive wastes penetrate the soil and accumulated inside due to Radioactivity.

h. Overgrazing and deforestation Overgrazing and clearing forest removes vegetations which cover the soil surface. Due to this, soil erosion occurs easily and topsoil layer which is rich in organic matter and nutrient is swept away by wind and water exposing infertile subsoil layer. Similarly, overgrazing and deforestation disturb soil microbial communities, nutrients cycling between soil and plants, and make soil compact decreasing water holding capacity and porosity.

2. EFFECTS OF SOIL POLLUTION i. Excessive use of biocides and chemical fertilizers in cropland make soil sterile thereby altering the physicochemical parameters of soil making it unfit for plants and animals. It causes insufficient and contaminated food supply to animals. ii. Soil pollution also affects air and water by making them polluted. iii. All organisms including human being come in contact with polluted soil containing heavy metals like lead, mercury which bring several genetic disorders, congenital illness and other health related issues such as cancer, eye problems, skin allergies, neurological disorder, urinary problems, gastro-intestinal disorder etc. iv. Pollutants like plastic rubber glasses etc. obstruct the nutrient absorption, disturbing plant physiology, growth and finally crop failure. v. Polluted soil is unfit for microbial community in the soil and its consequence is loss of all types of biodiversity like vegetation, insects, birds etc. from that area. vi. Polluted landscape or soil has no aesthetic and recreational value.
